author: Noki Doki
content: You can't tell the hierarchy from the vtable itself, the ctor and the dtor are usually good places to look

author: Noki Doki
content: Every time they write to the vtable field represents another class in the hierarchy (ctor has the base class before the derived class, dtor has them the other way around)

author: Noki Doki
content: In this case, the TAnimalBase ctor starts by calling the TSpineEnemy ctor, then only sets the TAnimalBase vtable after that, so TAnimalBase is a subclass of TSpineEnemy. It's important to look at vtable writes after the superclass ctor call, because some ctors are inlined

author: Noki Doki
content: If you repeat the process in the TSpineEnemy ctor, you see that TSpineEnemy extends TLiveActor, then in the TLiveActor ctor you see that TLiveActor extends TTakeActor, which in turns extends THitActor

author: Noki Doki
content: THitActor is the one that inherits two classes: JDrama::TPlacement and JDrama::TActor. You can also see the rest of the hierarchy right there because ctors are inlined all the way up (except JDrama::TNameRef but it doesn't inherit anything)
